tts: It is hard to imagine Italian food without tomatoes, Greek food without aubergines, or Thai food without peanut sauce. But before the sixteenth century these foods were not known outside South America.

They were first introduced to the rest of the world during a process known as the Columbian Exchange, named after Christopher Columbus: the exchange of food and other things between the New and Old Worlds.

Fruit and vegetables brought over from South and Central America included potatoes, tomatoes, sweetcorn, courgettes, aubergines, peanuts, pineapples, chillies and vanilla. Peanuts and chillies were then introduced to Asia by the Europeans.
It is estimated that sixty per cent of all the crops grown in the world today originated in the Americas.

items.q: What was the Columbian Exchange?
o: The exchange of foods between the New and Old Worlds

items.q: What proportion of the world’s crops originated in the Americas?
How did peanuts and chillies reach Asia?
o: They were introduced by the Europeans

tts: Nobody could have predicted this at the time, because initially the Europeans were not very enthusiastic about the new foods. It took three centuries before tomatoes and potatoes were accepted. People were suspicious of them, thinking they were dangerous to eat.
Both became very important crops in Europe by the nineteenth century. Ireland had become so dependent on potatoes that when the potato crop failed in the 1840s, a million people died of hunger.

The Americas gained many new foods from Europe in return, including apples, citrus fruit, lettuce, cucumber, onions, coffee, tea, wheat and rice. The Europeans also introduced cows to the New World. Before the exchange, Argentina — now so strongly associated with beef — had no cows, Mexican cuisine had no cheese, and Brazil had no coffee.
Quinoa, a grain grown in the Andes, has only in the last few years become hugely popular elsewhere. It is now considered a superfood, as it is extremely rich in protein.

items.s: Europeans were immediately enthusiastic about the new foods.
It took about three centuries for tomatoes and potatoes to be accepted.
Ireland had become heavily dependent on potatoes by the 1840s.
Argentina had cows before the Columbian Exchange.
Quinoa is described as rich in protein.

tts: Chillies are grown all over the world. They are from the same family as tomatoes, potatoes and aubergines. Although they make your mouth burn, they are also thought to have a number of health benefits: they can help with stomach problems and breathing problems, and can reduce the feeling of pain.

Vanilla is the most popular spice in the world. Its sweet, slightly smoky taste is often used in ice cream and other sweet dishes. It is the second most expensive spice on the market because it requires a great deal of hard labour to produce. For this reason it is sometimes referred to as green gold.

acts.title: The preposition that belongs to the adjective
rule: A great many English adjectives are followed by one preposition and no other. There is no rule to derive it from, and translation almost never helps, because the preposition is chosen by the English adjective rather than by the meaning. These have to be learnt as pairs.
points: Learn the pair, not the word
dependent ON, rich IN, aware OF, impressed BY, involved IN, responsible FOR, preferable TO.
A noun, a pronoun or an -ing form. Never an infinitive: responsible for organizing, not responsible for to organize.
impressed by / with are both used; impressed of is not. suspicious of, not suspicious about.
Both take an -ing form: keen on cooking, fussy about eating.
responsible FOR the delay = you caused it. responsible TO the manager = they are your boss.
eg: Many people are not aware of the risks.
I was not very impressed by the artwork.
Lots of countries were involved in the exchange.
Columbus was responsible for the start of it.
In a hot climate, hot tea is preferable to cold water.
People were suspicious of the new foods.
He is responsible for organizing the whole thing.
acts.careful: “responsible for to organize” is wrong, and so is “interested in to cook”. After a preposition the verb takes the -ing form. The only common exceptions are except and but, which take a bare infinitive: he did nothing except wait.

write.q: Write about 180 words on a food that your country is now strongly associated with but did not originally have — or one that arrived and never took. Use at least five adjective-plus-preposition pairs from this lesson, and make sure the verb after every preposition is an -ing form.
plan: the food, and where it actually came from
write.model:
Nothing here is more strongly associated with Kazakh food than the potato, and nothing in the kitchen is less native to it.

The potato originated in the Andes, arrived in the Russian empire in the eighteenth century, and reached the steppe with the settlers responsible for turning grassland into farmland. It was suspicious of nothing and nobody, but people were extremely suspicious of it, and for two generations it was fed mainly to animals.

What changed things was scarcity. By the middle of the last century a great many households were partly dependent on potatoes, because they store, they are rich in almost nothing except calories, and calories were the point.

Most people are not aware of any of this. Ask where the potato comes from and you will be told, without hesitation, that it is ours. Given how many families were involved in keeping each other fed with it, that answer is preferable to the accurate one, and I have stopped correcting it.
